children: Polish central banker Henryk Wnorowski said he is "certainly considering" the scenario of an interest rate hike in November, the PAP news agency reported on Monday.

Poland's central bank kept its main interest rate at 3.75% last Wednesday as inflation rose to 4.0% year on year in September, saying future decisions would depend on the outlook for prices and external factors, particularly commodity costs.

"I am certainly considering the scenario of an interest rate hike in November. It did not happen in October, although the September CPI reading of 4.0%, clearly above the upper deviation band, was an argument in favour of it," said Wnorowski, quoted by PAP.
The Governor of the National Bank of Poland Adam Glapinski said last week that forecasts indicate inflation in Poland could return to the central bank's target range of 1.5%–3.5% in October.

"However, in my view, even a return to the band does not mean that an interest rate hike will not be considered. In the current rapidly changing environment, the Council needs to take a more principled approach," Wnorowski said.
Glapinski also said the Monetary Policy Council was ready to act should inflation risks rise.
Asked whether the MPC might respond with an interest rate hike as early as November if the projection continues to show concerning data, he said: "Yes, although I do not foresee that."
